title: A Need Grows in Brooklyn
canon: Borough Park, Brooklyn, summer 1986. Marc is seventeen, sensitive, dreaming of acting at NYU, and gets pulled from petty mischief into the club-and-crime world of older dealers. Feature. NRC lead, (212) co-production. Live CMS canon, 2026-07-14.
look: Documentary realism on heavy 35mm grain. The lighting law, from the canon: two worlds with two kinds of light. THE BLOCK is daylight — natural, warm, unstyled, sun doing the work. THE CLUBS are after dark — the only light in frame is the room's own. A frame belongs to one world or the other; it never borrows the other's light.
note: Light Law pass 2026-07-18 — prompts from ANGIB_v6.fdx

stills.notes: INT. WEINSTEIN'S APPETIZERS & NUTS - PRE-DAWN - 5:55 AM. 'Frankie sets a side of salmon on the board and slides the long knife to Marc, handle first. A small ceremony.' / FRANKIE: 'Show me.' Why: the old world offering the boy its one inheritance before the club takes him — a knife passed handle first is a whole covenant in one gesture. Casting: canonical Marc = CU-marc.jpg (marc-labeled real photo). Al and Frankie are UNCAST; the prompt owns the old men. Store light is the location's own fluorescents; the street outside is still black.
stills.prompt: Inside Weinstein's Appetizers & Nuts, a fifty-year-old Jewish appetizing store in Borough Park, Brooklyn, before six on a summer morning in 1986. The store's own fluorescent tubes are the only light; the plate glass behind them is pre-dawn black. At the long wooden slicing board an old counterman, seventies, white hair, stained apron, sleeves rolled, slides a long lox knife across the board to Marc, seventeen, dark curls, an apron tied over a faded band t-shirt — the knife offered handle first, both of them looking down at it, a small ceremony. A side of salmon on the board, smoked fish on ice, bins of bulk nuts, faded photographs on the wall. Flat greenish tube light, deep shadow under the counter lip. Wide anamorphic composition. 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: EXT. UNDER THE EL - NEW UTRECHT AVENUE - DAY. 'Sunny grabs Marc's jacket, pulls him close, and yells something right in his face, full voice... the train eats every word of it. She's laughing.' / MARC (V.O.): 'She never did tell me. I got all the time in the world now, and that's still the thing I want'a know.' Why: the film's central unanswered sentence, held in one frame — she is saying it and it cannot be heard. Casting: Marc = CU-marc.jpg; the part of Sunny is played by the Chrissy files (blonde). Refs carry the two faces and wardrobe only.
stills.prompt: Under the elevated West End line on New Utrecht Avenue, Borough Park, Brooklyn, a hot summer afternoon in 1986, a train roaring over. Sunny, sixteen, teased blonde hair, jelly bracelets, denim vest over a tank top, has grabbed the front of Marc's cut-off denim jacket in both fists and pulled him close, yelling something full-voice right into his face, laughing while she does it. Marc, seventeen, dark curls, a paper cup of Italian ice in one hand, caught between laughing and straining to hear — the train is eating every word. Hard noon sun drops through the tracks in stripes, bright bars and black shadow crossing the two of them, warm bounce off parked sedans. Steel pillars, storefront awnings running off behind. Wide anamorphic composition. 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT. MARC'S HOUSE - NIGHT (the house-party sequence). 'Down on the stoop stands Sunny, dressed up nice, hugging her elbows.' / 'She steps back off the stoop and looks up, right at the dark window.' / 'Marc holds dead still behind the curtain, an inch of glass between them.' Why: the whole tragedy in one inch of glass — he hides from the one person who came for him. Casting: Marc = CU-marc.jpg; Sunny = Chrissy files. Refs carry faces and wardrobe only; the dark room and the streetlamp belong to the prompt.
stills.prompt: A dark upstairs front room of a Borough Park rowhouse on a summer night in 1986. No lamp is on; the only light climbs in from the sodium streetlight outside, a weak amber wash on the ceiling and the lace curtain. Marc, seventeen, dark curls, shirt half open, stands dead still at the window, holding the curtain's edge open one inch, his face caught in that thin warm stripe, the rest of him black. Down through the glass, small on the sidewalk below, Sunny, sixteen, blonde, dressed up nice, stands under the streetlamp hugging her elbows, looking straight up at the dark window — at him. Parked sedans, stoops, the block asleep. Wide anamorphic composition, the dark room heavy around the boy, the lit girl small below. 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT. HIGH SCHOOL AUDITORIUM - NIGHT. 'In the third row, an empty seat with a coat saved over it. Beside it, SUNNY, dressed up, a little program rolled in her hands.' / 'She watches the wrong boy say Marc's lines. She doesn't cry. She just sits very still.' Why: absence made visible — a girl, a saved seat, and the part he threw away happening onstage without him. Casting: Sunny = the Chrissy files; Marc is not in this frame, so no Marc ref. The auditorium's only light is the stage's own spill.
stills.prompt: A Brooklyn public high school auditorium on a night in 1986, mid-performance of the school play. In the third row of wooden fold-down seats sits Sunny, sixteen, teased blonde hair, dressed up, a small paper program rolled tight in both hands. She sits very still, eyes on the stage out of frame — not crying, watching the way you watch something you already know the end of. Beside her, a folded coat saved over an empty seat, for someone who is not coming. Scattered parents in the dark rows behind. The only light in the house is the stage wash spilling back over the first rows, warm on her face and the folded coat, dying to black behind her. Wide anamorphic composition. 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT. MARC'S HOUSE - KITCHEN - NIGHT. FRANCINE: 'Then look at me and tell me it's clean.' / 'Marc opens his mouth. Looks at her. Can't do it. His eyes go to the floor.' / 'She leaves the sixty dollars sitting on the table between them.' Why: mother and son severed by three twenties — the price of the club sitting on formica, the one thing in the house nobody will touch. Casting: Marc = CU-marc.jpg. Francine is UNCAST — MammaModella.jpg exists in 02-stills/ref as a candidate but needs Marco's ruling; until then the prompt owns her.
stills.prompt: The kitchen of a Borough Park rowhouse late on a night in 1986. Francine, early fifties, a nurse still in her whites, the permanent kind of tired in her face, stands at the formica table, textbook and glasses gathered against her, looking at her son. Marc, seventeen, dark curls, silk shirt under a denim jacket, stands across the table, eyes gone down to the worn linoleum, unable to hold her look. Between them on the table: three twenty-dollar bills, squared into a neat stack neither will touch. The only light is the room's own fixture over the table, hard warm down-light pooling on the money, dropping both faces half into shadow; the window over the sink is black. Wide anamorphic composition. 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: EXT. LIMELIGHT - ROPES - NIGHT. 'an OLD MAN in a fish-store apron... Frankie Cashman from Weinstein's, white hair, out of place, walking his little dog past the club.' / 'Frankie gives the smallest nod... not approval, acknowledgment, the saddest kind.' / 'For one beat the lengthened posture goes out of him and he's just a boy caught.' Why: the two worlds of the film meet on one sidewalk and hold a look too long — the morning kid seen inside the night kid. Casting: Marc = CU-marc.jpg; Frankie is UNCAST, the prompt owns him. Night world: the only light is the club's own and one streetlamp.
stills.prompt: The sidewalk outside the Limelight on Sixth Avenue at 20th Street, New York, the middle of a night in 1986 — the deconsecrated Gothic brownstone church running as a nightclub. Marc, seventeen, dark curls, in club black with a clipboard at the velvet rope, has stopped picking faces. Down the sidewalk an old man has stopped too: white hair, a fish-store apron under an open coat, a little dog on a leash, out of place in the club line. Across the crowd the two hold each other's eyes — the boy caught, the old man giving the smallest nod there is. No daylight anywhere: warm gold spills from the Gothic doorway onto Marc; one cold streetlamp holds the old man, the crowd between them falling to black. Wide anamorphic composition. 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: EXT. UNDER THE EL - NEW UTRECHT AVENUE - WINTER - DAY. SUNNY: 'You don't listen for the train. The steel knows first.' / 'They stand there, two hands flat on a frozen pillar, breath coming out in clouds.' / 'Her hand is steady on the steel. His hand is shaking. She looks at his hand. She keeps hers where it is.' Why: the last time they touch — the addiction confessed by a hand, and her answer is to keep hers where it is. Casting: Marc = CU-marc.jpg; Sunny = Chrissy files. Refs carry faces and wardrobe only.
stills.prompt: Under the El on New Utrecht Avenue, Borough Park, Brooklyn, a flat gray December day in 1988. Close on a steel pillar of the elevated line, rivets and chipped green paint: two bare hands laid flat on the frozen steel, side by side. Hers, a teenage girl's, jelly bracelets pushed down the wrist, steady. His, a boy's, shaking. Soft behind the hands, the two of them: Sunny, blonde, scarf and winter coat, looking down at his hand; Marc, dark curls, silk shirt under a leather jacket, no scarf, looking away up the tracks. Breath hangs in clouds. Christmas lights strung pillar to pillar overhead, half the bulbs working, weak color against an overcast sky. Flat even winter light, no sun anywhere. Wide anamorphic composition. 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.

stills.notes: INT. CLUB - DANCE FLOOR - NIGHT. 'Millie goes down on her knees and gets sick on the floor in front of everyone.' / 'Marc gets his arms under her and picks her up off the floor, all of her, and stands there holding her while the crowd laughs at the both of them now.' Why: the one decent act he has left, performed in front of a laughing room — tenderness against a wall of noise. Casting: Marc = CU-marc.jpg. Millie is UNCAST; the page owns her: dark hair, white dress, one shoe gone, mascara everywhere. Night world — nothing in this frame is lit from outside the room.
stills.prompt: The dance floor of the Limelight, New York, the middle of a night in 1989, inside the deconsecrated Gothic church. The packed crowd has opened into a ring; at its center Marc, dark curls, black silk shirt, holds a teenage girl clean off the floor in both arms — dark hair wrecked, white dress finished, one shoe gone, mascara down her face, her head rolled against his chest. Around the ring the crowd points and laughs, faces caught mid-jeer. He is the only still thing in the room. The room is sealed; the only light is the club's own — colored beams raking through haze, a strobe at the ring's edge, a red wash over the laughing faces, stone arches vanishing into black overhead. Wide anamorphic composition. 35mm film still, heavy natural grain. No text, no watermark.
